scope_summary: Finish coat application (typically 2 coats) on primed drywall wall surfaces in new construction. Assumes primer is cured and surface is ready. Does NOT include primer application, ceiling finish, or trim finish.
relevant_findings: Standard NC finish is 2 coats of latex paint over primed drywall
1-coat finish is acceptable for economy/QT2 work or touch-up scenarios only
Sheen selection impacts quality tier minimum: Semi-gloss/gloss requires QT4+ per doctrine
Spray+backroll is dominant method in NC production — uses 18-inch roller per doctrine
Sanding between coats: None for QT2, spot-sand patches for QT3, full sand for QT4/QT5
Floor protection scope varies: NC with unfinished floors = minimal; finished floors = full protection
Edge work complexity increases when trim is already installed and finished
Proper dry time between coats is critical — typically 2-4 hours depending on conditions

prep_requirements_over_primer.method: Walk with work light, check for holidays, sags, dust nibs
prep_requirements_over_primer.reason: Primer defects telegraph through finish coats

prep_requirements_over_primer.method: Tack cloth or damp rag wipe
prep_requirements_over_primer.reason: Construction dust settles on primer before finish application
prep_requirements_over_primer.skip_conditions: QT2 may reduce to spot check

prep_requirements_over_primer.method: 120 grit sanding block or pole sander
prep_requirements_over_primer.reason: Improves adhesion, per Quality Tiers doctrine

prep_requirements_over_primer.method: 120-150 grit pole sander for walls, block for detail
prep_requirements_over_primer.reason: Required per Quality Tiers doctrine for enhanced prep

prep_requirements_over_primer.method: Brush-apply primer to any missed spots or repairs
prep_requirements_over_primer.reason: Ensure uniform absorption before finish coats
prep_requirements_over_primer.skip_conditions: Only if defects found during inspection

QT3.between_finish_coats: Spot sand patches only if necessary

QT4.between_finish_coats: Spot sand as needed + full sand between coats

QT5.notes: More scrutiny on inspection and patchwork. Slower working speed.

rules.notes: Economy sheens, forgiving of surface imperfections
Higher sheens require enhanced prep and sanding

sheen_quality_tier_requirements.automatic_upgrade: If requested sheen exceeds quality tier maximum, upgrade quality tier automatically

sheen_production_impacts.hide_capability: Very good — slight sheen, good hide
Good — soft luster, reveals some imperfections

sheen_production_impacts.typical_use: Trim, doors, rarely for walls except commercial

when_appropriate: Very light color change (same sheen family)
one_coat.coverage_expectation: May show primer bleed-through, uneven sheen
one_coat.warranty_impact: Most manufacturers require 2 coats for warranty

two_coat.coverage_expectation: Full hide, uniform sheen, proper film build

texture_impact_on_finish.sheen_notes: All sheens work well, higher sheens look best on smooth
Flat/matte hide texture peaks, higher sheens accentuate texture
Flat/matte strongly preferred, satin+ can look plastic

spray_backroll_roller_size.rule: Use 18-inch roller frame and nap for spray+backroll systems
spray_backroll_roller_size.rationale: Larger roller width increases backroll production, enabling faster overall throughput since spray is coupled to backroll
spray_backroll_roller_size.application: Standard for production spray+backroll on walls and ceilings in new construction

common_failure_modes.cause: Not maintaining wet edge, too slow application, wrong sheen technique
common_failure_modes.prevention: Work quickly in sections, maintain wet edge, use extender for higher sheens
common_failure_modes.remediation: Sand and recoat, may require full room redo for high sheen

common_failure_modes.cause: Wrong nap length, overworking paint, paint too thick
common_failure_modes.prevention: Use appropriate nap (3/8" for smooth), proper loading, don't overwork
common_failure_modes.remediation: Sand lightly and recoat with proper technique

common_failure_modes.cause: Inconsistent film thickness, spot touch-ups, poor primer coverage
common_failure_modes.prevention: Uniform application, full coat coverage, address primer issues first
common_failure_modes.remediation: Additional full coat, may need to reprime patched areas

common_failure_modes.cause: Contaminated primer surface, insufficient dry time, incompatible products
common_failure_modes.prevention: Clean primer surface, follow recoat times, use compatible system
common_failure_modes.remediation: Remove loose paint, sand, spot prime, recoat

common_failure_modes.cause: Airborne dust settling in wet paint, contaminated rollers
common_failure_modes.prevention: Control dust, use clean applicators, adequate HVAC filtration

common_failure_modes.cause: Mixing paint from different batches, inconsistent coverage
common_failure_modes.prevention: Box paint from multiple containers, full coat coverage

required_paintscope_keys.required_when: Always for QT3+ (edge work always required for finish coats)
When trim is installed before wall finish

required_paintscope_keys.description: Floor area requiring protection during painting
required_paintscope_keys.required_when: When finished flooring is installed before wall painting

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Cut-in required if ceiling is different color or already finished
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Ceilings typically finished before walls in NC
Sequence varies: some NC has trim installed but not finished
NC typically has subfloor only during painting

assumptions: Primer is properly cured (minimum 24 hours, ideally 2-7 days)
Primer is compatible with finish paint
uncertainties: Exact production impact of higher sheens varies by product
Recoat windows vary by manufacturer and conditions
Floor protection scope in NC varies by builder requirements
